jobs.description:
About The Role

GFL is seeking a visionary, high-energy leader with a passion for financial modeling, advanced analytics, and commercial business insights. Are you a strategic leader who thrives at the intersection of complex data, technology, and executive strategy? As the Director of Business Analytics, you will drive our enterprise-wide intelligence roadmap and foster a high-impact, data-driven culture across our fast-paced, high-growth organization.

This is a newly created position driven by our consistent expansion, appetite for data-driven decision-making, and relentless push for continuous improvement. You will join our leadership team at an exceptionally exciting time as we’ve embarked on our pricing program transformation, placing you at the forefront of this value creating engagement. Working with a "no can't do" attitude, you will translate complex technical data into compelling commercial narratives that shape global corporate strategy and optimize bottom-line performance.

Key Responsibilities

Reporting directly to the VP, Operations Strategy, you will lead a dynamic team to drive performance and deliver value-added decision support across the business. Key responsibilities include:

Pricing Excellence: Assess enterprise pricing performance, build advanced pricing models from scratch, identify margin opportunities, and challenge assumptions. Influence Area Vice Presidents and Business Unit leaders to translate analytical insights into actionable strategies that optimize commercial outcomes.
Advanced Analytics & AI: Champion statistical modeling, machine learning, and predictive analytics to transition the business from descriptive reporting to prescriptive intelligence. Accelerate speed-to-insight by integrating modern analytics tools, AWS-native workflows, predictive machine learning, and responsible GenAI/copilots.
Strategic Roadmap Development: Define and execute the long-term vision for the Business Analytics department. Scale enterprise data platforms and ensure full alignment between analytics initiatives and global corporate objectives.
Operational Excellence: Oversee the full data lifecycle—from ingestion and pipeline collaboration to the delivery of interactive executive dashboards, automated workflows, and high-impact predictive tools.
Data Governance & Integrity: Establish rigorous standards for data quality, security, and governance. Define control frameworks and KPIs to ensure business intelligence is accurate, reliable, and meeting compliance benchmarks.
Stakeholder Influence: Partner closely with Operations, Sales, Marketing, and Finance leadership. Translate ambiguous operational and market questions into clear recommendations, guiding executive partners through trade-offs with decision-ready narratives.
Team Leadership: Hire, coach, and retain a high-performing team of analysts and data professionals. Foster a culture of continuous improvement, analytical rigor, and collaborative business partnering.

Qualifications

10+ years of progressive experience in analytics, data science, or related quantitative fields, including experimentation frameworks, statistical modeling, and time-series analysis.
5+ years in pricing, revenue management, or applied data science within B2B or service-oriented industries, with a proven track record of building dynamic pricing and financial models from scratch.
5+ years of people management experience, including structuring team processes for service delivery in fast-paced environments, presenting to C-suite audiences, and driving cross-functional alignment.
Expert-level modeling skills and hands-on proficiency with major BI tools (Power BI, QuickSight, Tableau) and database querying (SQL).
Direct experience with AWS cloud data environments (e.g., S3, Glue, Athena, Forecast, or SageMaker) and leveraging GenAI/copilots to accelerate insight generation.
Executive Communication & Influence: Exceptional ability to distill complex data insights into concise, persuasive presentations for senior leaders.
Commercial & Financial Acumen: Deep understanding of operational finance, FP&A, and business operations, with the ability to link data metrics directly to bottom-line profitability.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Finance, Economics, Statistics, or Computer Science required; Master’s degree in a quantitative field highly preferred.

jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?

The Senior Director, Data Architecture simplifies and unifies RBC's data architecture across the full lifecycle: manufacturing, distribution, discovery, consumption and governance. They own the target data architecture, the RBC Lumina reference architecture and the standards that make data machine-readable for people, applications and AI agents.

Success means fewer data stores and point-to-point feeds, one trusted source for each critical data element, and data products agents can find and use within their entitlements.

What will you do?

Manufacturing (data sources). Name the authoritative source for every critical data element. Own the canonical data model and business glossary alignment. Set the standard for producer data contracts covering schema, semantics, quality rules and SLAs, so quality is fixed at the source.
Distribution (RBC Lumina). Own the Lumina reference architecture and the standard ingestion patterns: batch, streaming, CDC, events and APIs. Move data once, reliably and traceably. Run the roadmap to retire point-to-point interfaces.
Discovery and machine readability. Define what counts as a data product and the minimum metadata each must carry: meaning, owner, lineage, quality and entitlements. Build the semantic layer and ontology that lets agents interpret data, not just locate it. Set the agent-access pattern for data products, such as MCP.
Consumption. Define the consumption archetypes (BI, operational APIs, analytics and ML, RAG, agents) with one supported pattern for each. Feed curated, entitlement-aware data products into the common RAG substrate.
Governance by design. Act as design authority through architecture review, decision records and exceptions. Partner with the CDO, who owns policy and accountability, while this role owns how standards are built in. Support BCBS 239 lineage and jurisdiction-aware data placement for sovereignty.
Simplification and transformation. Inventory data platforms, stores and tools across RBC's stacks and give each a disposition: tolerate, invest, migrate or eliminate. Tie the roadmap to in-flight programs such as Finance Modernization and AML Transformation, and to third-party rationalization.

What do you need to succeed?

15+ years in data architecture or data engineering, including 5+ years leading architects at enterprise scale.
Depth across lakehouse and warehouse platforms, streaming and CDC, data products and mesh, catalogs and metadata, semantic layers and knowledge graphs.
A track record of measurable simplification: platforms retired, feeds removed and costs taken out.
Working knowledge of BCBS 239, privacy regulation and OSFI expectations for data risk.
Clear view on making data AI-ready, including retrieval, entitlement propagation and agent access.
Able to align the CDO, platform engineering and business data owners without direct authority over them.

Job Description

What is the opportunity?

This leader sets one standard way to build, secure and run AI across RBC Technology & Operations. They own the reference architecture for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), AI agents, model access and AI-native software delivery (AI-DLC). The role turns the 2030 T&O ambitions, including AI-native delivery and 30% of GenAI volume on open-weight models, into patterns teams actually use.

Success means fewer bespoke stacks, faster delivery with maintainable code, and AI that Internal Audit, Model Risk and OSFI can trust.

What will you do
?

AI architecture standards as code. Define the enterprise AI reference architecture and approved patterns. Encode them as harness skills, agent constitutions and automated fitness checks, so standards apply at generation time rather than at review.
Common RAG substrate. Converge the many RAG solutions onto one shared platform: ingestion, chunking, embeddings, hybrid retrieval, reranking and evaluation. Retrieval must respect source entitlements by default. Set a retirement plan for duplicate stacks.
Agent sandboxing and security architecture. Design the sandbox standard for every agentic workload: ephemeral environments, egress allow-lists, short-lived task-scoped credentials and no standing production access. Own agent identity, tool access through a governed MCP gateway and registry, and defenses against prompt injection and poisoned tools.
AI-DLC harness and quality gates. Own the harness architecture from spec to release. Make quality gates deterministic and mandatory: tests and coverage, static analysis, complexity and duplication limits, dependency and license checks, security scanning and architecture fitness checks. Enforce separation of duties (the agent that writes a change cannot approve it), PR size limits and traceability from spec to deployment.
Skills and evaluation lifecycle. Treat skills like code: owned, versioned, regression-tested with evals and retired when stale. Re-run evals before any model upgrade reaches teams.
Model gateway and inference architecture. Route work across frontier and open-weight models by cost, risk and jurisdiction. Build in token metering, caching and data-classification rules so cost and residency are enforced by the platform.
Risk-tiered control model. Partner with Internal Audit, Model Risk and Cyber to define human-oversight tiers, from human-on-the-loop for low-risk work to human-in-the-loop for payments and core banking. Align with OSFI Guidelines E-23 and B-13.
Design authority and innovation. Chair AI architecture review, keep decision records and manage exceptions. Graduate proven lab work into the platform and evaluate emerging technology, such as agent protocols and new open-weight models.

What do you need to succeed?

15+ years in architecture or engineering, including 5+ years leading architects or engineers at enterprise scale.
Hands-on depth in LLM systems: RAG, agent frameworks, MCP, evaluation and inference serving on cloud and on-premises GPUs.
Security architecture for AI, including the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications, sandboxing and identity for non-human actors.
Strong DevSecOps and SDLC background; you have shipped quality gates engineers accepted rather than routed around.
Experience in a regulated industry, ideally financial services under OSFI.
Credibility with engineers: you still prototype and read code. Able to explain trade-offs plainly to executives and audit.

The Director of Finance is also accountable for compliance with financial regulations and standards. They must ensure that all financial transactions and operations within the department adhere to the Financial Administrative Manual (FAM) as well as legal and ethical guidelines.

The main responsibilities of the Director are, but are not limited to:

Leading the process of developing the department's annual budget, working with program managers and finance staff to gather input, projections, and cost estimates;
Facilitating the budget approval process, working closely with government agencies, legislative bodies, and stakeholders to address questions, concerns, and revisions;
Overseeing the allocation and execution of budgeted funds, ensuring that expenditures are in line with approved allocations and regulatory guidelines;
Managing the process for budget amendments or revisions as necessary, providing clear justifications and seeking necessary approvals for changes;
Ensuring that all financial reports meet regulatory requirements and government accounting principles, providing transparency and accountability in financial disclosures;
Establishing and maintaining robust internal controls to safeguard financial assets, prevent fraud, and ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial data;
Overseeing and leading a team of financial professionals, providing guidance, mentorship, and support to promote their professional growth and ensure effective departmental operations;
Fostering a culture of collaboration and cross-functional teamwork, working closely with other department heads to ensure financial considerations are integrated into broader strategic planning.

Undergraduate degree in accounting, finance, business administration, economics, commerce, or related field;
Completion of a professional accounting designation CPA (CMA, CGA or CA);
Eight (8) years of related experience;
Five (5) years of progressive managerial experience in assigning priorities and managing performance of professional teams.

The Director, IT leads day-to-day delivery of technology services and operational security. Reporting to the VP Finance, IT and Risk, this role is YWCA's senior technology leader, setting technology direction and translating it into execution by running reliable IT operations and strengthening cybersecurity controls that protect YWCA’s clients, staff, and organisational reputation.

Reports to:
Vice President, Finance, IT and Risk
Direct reports:
Senior IT Systems Manager, plus additional technical staff as required
Governance:
provides operational metrics and risk updates to the VP Finance, IT and Risk; participates in cross-functional governance forums as required

Delegated authority and decision rights

Runs day-to-day operations across sites, including escalation pathways, on-call structure, service workflows, and operational communications to staff.
Approves routine operational changes, configuration standards enforcement, and remediation plans (patching, vulnerability remediation coordination, endpoint baselines) consistent with standards approved by the VP Finance, IT and Risk.
Recommends technology standards, policies, and the annual IT operating and capital budget for approval by the VP Finance, IT and Risk.
Defines and enforces operational processes (incident/problem/change), service catalogue structure, and operational metrics.
Manages renewals, service performance, and vendor issue escalation; can approve vendor work orders and operational purchases within budget and delegated signing limits.
Owns operational control implementation and upkeep (monitoring, endpoint protection, email protections, conditional access operations) and ensures evidence is maintained for audits and cyber insurance.
Leads performance management, scheduling, coverage planning, and hiring for operational roles (with VP Finance, IT and Risk approval for net-new roles or material restructuring).

What you’ll be doing:

1) IT operations and service management

Run day-to-day IT operations, ensuring stable services, responsive support, and clear escalation pathways for front-line teams.
Implement service management practices, including ticketing workflows, incident and problem management, and change coordination.
Define and track operational performance metrics (for example, ticket volumes, time to resolution, recurring issues) and drive continuous improvement.

2) Infrastructure, platforms, and endpoint management

Oversee network, connectivity, collaboration, and core cloud services to ensure availability, security, and supportability.
Ensure consistent execution of endpoint management, patching, configuration standards, and identity and access operations (including Joiner-Mover-Leaver (JML) processes and access reviews).
Support the operational health of data pipelines and BI tools, ensuring data sources are reliable and accessible for enterprise reporting.
Provide operational support for network-connected physical security systems (e.g., CCTV, access control).
Oversee configuration, support, and integration of core business applications (e.g., client management, finance, and HR systems), working with system owners across the organisation.
Maintain backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity capabilities for critical systems, including regular restore testing.

3) Vendor, procurement, and asset management

Own the device and asset lifecycle program: standards, procurement coordination, tagging, inventory accuracy, deployment, transfers, replacements, secure wiping, and disposal.
Enforce mobile and BYOD access controls appropriate to risk, including limitations on local storage and expectations for incident reporting, remote wipe, and support boundaries.
Manage operational vendor relationships, renewals, and service performance, escalating risks and material issues to the VP Finance, IT and Risk.
Manage the IT operating and capital budget, including license and subscription costs, and report on spending against plan.

4) Cybersecurity operations and control implementation

Operationalise security controls and maintain security tooling configurations and monitoring across endpoints, networks, and cloud services.
Coordinate vulnerability management, including scanning, risk-based prioritisation, and remediation tracking.
Maintain operational readiness for incidents, including runbooks, escalation, evidence preservation support, and post-incident corrective actions.
Apply privacy and safety safeguards to systems that hold sensitive client information, and support privacy impact assessments and breach response.
Maintain IT policies and staff guidance (e.g., acceptable use) and deliver security awareness training, including phishing simulations.

5) Project delivery and change enablement

Lead delivery of operational technology projects (upgrades, migrations, tooling improvements), managing scope, timelines, and stakeholder communication.
Work with program leaders to translate needs into feasible solutions and sustainable support models.
Ensure changes are adopted successfully through training, communications, and transition to steady-state operations.
Develop and maintain the multi-year technology roadmap in partnership with the VP Finance, IT and Risk, and translate it into actionable project plans, ensuring operational readiness for all new deployments.

6) People leadership

Lead, coach, and develop the IT operations team, including performance management, training plans, and coverage planning.
Establish clear on-call, escalation, and handoff practices that protect staff wellbeing and maintain service reliability.

Required experience and capabilities

8+ years of progressive IT experience, including leadership of infrastructure and end-user computing in a multi-site environment.
Demonstrated experience operating and improving IT service delivery, including ticketing, incident management, and operational metrics.
Practical cybersecurity experience, including patching discipline, endpoint security, identity and access practices, and incident response support.
Strong vendor and contract operations capability, including renewals, service performance management, and procurement coordination.
Ability to communicate clearly with non-technical stakeholders and drive adoption of consistent practices.
People leadership experience, including coaching, performance management, and coverage planning for reliable operations.
Experience developing multi-year technology roadmaps and managing IT budgets.
Post-secondary degree or diploma in information technology, computer science, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Preferred experience

Experience in non-profit, housing, or human services environments with heightened privacy and safety considerations.
ITIL or comparable service management training, and project delivery experience (formal or practical).

Working conditions

Based in Metro Vancouver with occasional travel to multiple sites as required.
Hybrid work may be supported depending on operational needs, incident readiness, and leadership expectations.
This role participates in incident response leadership and may require after-hours availability for critical incidents and scheduled maintenance windows.

Reporting to the Executive Director, Corporate Services, the Director, Finance (Director) is the senior financial advisor for the Department of Health. The position is responsible for the financial stewardship and accountability of public funds administered by Health. At the core of their duties is the oversight of the department’s capital and operations and maintenance budget, ensuring that financial resources are allocated efficiently and in accordance with government policies and regulations. The Director of Finance is also accountable for compliance with financial regulations and standards. They must ensure that all financial transactions and operations within the department adhere to the Financial Administrative Manual (FAM) as well as legal and ethical guidelines.

The main responsibilities of the Director are, but are not limited to:

Leading the process of developing the department's annual budget, working with program managers and finance staff to gather input, projections, and cost estimates;
Facilitating the budget approval process, working closely with government agencies, legislative bodies, and stakeholders to address questions, concerns, and revisions;
Overseeing the allocation and execution of budgeted funds, ensuring that expenditures are in line with approved allocations and regulatory guidelines;
Managing the process for budget amendments or revisions as necessary, providing clear justifications and seeking necessary approvals for changes;
Ensuring that all financial reports meet regulatory requirements and government accounting principles, providing transparency and accountability in financial disclosures;
Establishing and maintaining robust internal controls to safeguard financial assets, prevent fraud, and ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial data;
Overseeing and leading a team of financial professionals, providing guidance, mentorship, and support to promote their professional growth and ensure effective departmental operations;
Fostering a culture of collaboration and cross-functional teamwork, working closely with other department heads to ensure financial considerations are integrated into broader strategic planning.

The knowledge, skills, and abilities required for this job are usually obtained through a recognized:

Undergraduate degree in accounting, finance, business administration, economics, commerce, or related field;
Completion of a professional accounting designation CPA (CMA, CGA or CA);
Eight (8) years of related experience;
Five (5) years of progressive managerial experience in assigning priorities and managing performance of professional teams.

This is a Position of Trust and a satisfactory Criminal Record Check is required.

Reports to:
Vice President, Finance, IT and Risk
Direct reports:
Senior IT Systems Manager, plus additional technical staff as required
Governance:
provides operational metrics and risk updates to the VP Finance, IT and Risk; participates in cross-functional governance forums as required

Delegated authority and decision rights

Runs day-to-day operations across sites, including escalation pathways, on-call structure, service workflows, and operational communications to staff.
Approves routine operational changes, configuration standards enforcement, and remediation plans (patching, vulnerability remediation coordination, endpoint baselines) consistent with standards approved by the VP Finance, IT and Risk.
Recommends technology standards, policies, and the annual IT operating and capital budget for approval by the VP Finance, IT and Risk.
Defines and enforces operational processes (incident/problem/change), service catalogue structure, and operational metrics.
Manages renewals, service performance, and vendor issue escalation; can approve vendor work orders and operational purchases within budget and delegated signing limits.
Owns operational control implementation and upkeep (monitoring, endpoint protection, email protections, conditional access operations) and ensures evidence is maintained for audits and cyber insurance.
Leads performance management, scheduling, coverage planning, and hiring for operational roles (with VP Finance, IT and Risk approval for net-new roles or material restructuring).

What you’ll be doing:

1) IT operations and service management

Run day-to-day IT operations, ensuring stable services, responsive support, and clear escalation pathways for front-line teams.
Implement service management practices, including ticketing workflows, incident and problem management, and change coordination.
Define and track operational performance metrics (for example, ticket volumes, time to resolution, recurring issues) and drive continuous improvement.

2) Infrastructure, platforms, and endpoint management

Oversee network, connectivity, collaboration, and core cloud services to ensure availability, security, and supportability.
Ensure consistent execution of endpoint management, patching, configuration standards, and identity and access operations (including Joiner-Mover-Leaver (JML) processes and access reviews).
Support the operational health of data pipelines and BI tools, ensuring data sources are reliable and accessible for enterprise reporting.
Provide operational support for network-connected physical security systems (e.g., CCTV, access control).
Oversee configuration, support, and integration of core business applications (e.g., client management, finance, and HR systems), working with system owners across the organisation.
Maintain backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity capabilities for critical systems, including regular restore testing.

3) Vendor, procurement, and asset management

Own the device and asset lifecycle program: standards, procurement coordination, tagging, inventory accuracy, deployment, transfers, replacements, secure wiping, and disposal.
Enforce mobile and BYOD access controls appropriate to risk, including limitations on local storage and expectations for incident reporting, remote wipe, and support boundaries.
Manage operational vendor relationships, renewals, and service performance, escalating risks and material issues to the VP Finance, IT and Risk.
Manage the IT operating and capital budget, including license and subscription costs, and report on spending against plan.

4) Cybersecurity operations and control implementation

Operationalise security controls and maintain security tooling configurations and monitoring across endpoints, networks, and cloud services.
Coordinate vulnerability management, including scanning, risk-based prioritisation, and remediation tracking.
Maintain operational readiness for incidents, including runbooks, escalation, evidence preservation support, and post-incident corrective actions.
Apply privacy and safety safeguards to systems that hold sensitive client information, and support privacy impact assessments and breach response.
Maintain IT policies and staff guidance (e.g., acceptable use) and deliver security awareness training, including phishing simulations.

5) Project delivery and change enablement

Lead delivery of operational technology projects (upgrades, migrations, tooling improvements), managing scope, timelines, and stakeholder communication.
Work with program leaders to translate needs into feasible solutions and sustainable support models.
Ensure changes are adopted successfully through training, communications, and transition to steady-state operations.
Develop and maintain the multi-year technology roadmap in partnership with the VP Finance, IT and Risk, and translate it into actionable project plans, ensuring operational readiness for all new deployments.

The Sr. Director Product & Platform Trust is accountable for shaping how Autodesk product teams build safe and secure products at scale. Experience improving security remediation at scale by addressing developer workflow, tooling, automation, or other systemic barriers
Strong understanding of modern software development practices, cloud and platform architectures, secure software development lifecycle practices, and application security techniques
Experience leading multidisciplinary organizations that include security practitioners and engineering and/or product management functions
